thread:
matt-client: Hey support — customer reports a 400 on /v1/embeddings when sending batches. Works for other customers. Error message: \"400 Bad Request: invalid input shape\". They sent 3 items, got 3 failures and a billing spike from retries. Any hints?

sarah-support: Ugh. Can you paste the exact payload (no secrets) and the model name? Also request_id if you have it.

matt-client: Model: text-embed-1536 (internal). Request id: req_8f3b2a17. Payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  "input": "[\"How to deploy\", \"Install guide\", \"Troubleshooting\"]",
  "model": "text-embed-1536"
}
```

matt-client: Notice we accidentally stringified the array on the client. The JS client was doing JSON.stringify(inputs) before sending.

sarah-support: That explains it. Server expects either ["str1","str2"] or [[f1,f2,...],[...]] for vectors. If you send a single string that contains brackets it gets parsed as one item (string) — model validate sees wrong type.

alex-ml: Quick clarification: if the server receives a single string that looks like an array, we currently treat it as a single text input, not a parsed list. So downstream embedding code attempts tokenization and embedding — fine — but if the customer sent arrays-of-numbers as stringified JSON, that triggers the \"expected floats\" branch and we return 400 with shape info.

matt-client: The customer actually has two client variants. One sends strings, one sends precomputed vectors but stringified. The stringified vectors produced: "[0.001, -0.23, ...]" and we ended up with a dimension mismatch: error said expected 1536 but got 1535 for one element.

sarah-support: Can you repro locally? Short repro steps are useful for ops.

matt-client: Repro steps (JS fetch):
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer x', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'text-embed-1536', input: JSON.stringify(['hello','world']) })
})
```
This returns 400 — expected. If input is not stringified it succeeds.

olivia-sre: Posting for visibility — we saw a transient spike in 5xxs and rate-limit responses from that customer's token earlier, correlates with rapid retries after the client code got 400s. Can you confirm if retries were immediate?

matt-client: Yes, client lib had aggressive retry on network errors and also retried on non-200 because they used a naive wrapper. It retried 6 times quickly, causing billing and throttle.

sarah-support: Two asks: 1) ask customer to stop sending stringified arrays and patch client to send proper JSON list; 2) we should improve error message/server-side validation to catch stringified arrays and return a clear message like \"input must be an array of strings or arrays of numbers, not a JSON-string\" to reduce retries.

alex-ml: Agreed. Proposed quick server check: if input is a string and it looks like a JSON array (starts with '[' and ends with ']'), return 400 with guidance and error_code: INPUT_STRINGIFIED_ARRAY. That avoids downstream dimension confusion. I'll file a tiny PR.

olivia-sre: Also add a short-term throttling rule per API key to avoid billing spikes from client-side bugs — set retry-backoff recommendation in docs. I can add a monitoring alert for repeated 400s+retries pattern.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: patch/validate-stringified-array -> staging at 2072511000, prod after 30m smoke.

sarah-support: I emailed the customer with repro snippet, asked them to stop auto-retrying on 4xx and push a fix to not stringify input. I'll follow up after deploy.

matt-client: Thanks all — will coordinate customer patch and confirm once done.

olivia-sre: Follow-up: after patch we saw request_id req_8f3b2a17 get retried -> dropped; no further billing anomalies, alert tuned. Closing loop tomorrow unless regressions found. :thumbsup:
